case.summary: Verdict is uncertain at probability 0.35 for card C03042-K1, candidate pattern account_takeover: a four-transaction episode inside 48 hours (3462385, 3462387, 3462404 in-person at the card's home region 299.0 on 2016-11-16, then the flagged online purchase 3464869 for $599.94 on 2016-11-17) totaling $2,140.94 exposure. The decisive fraud-side evidence (history family) is the chain itself — an in-person spree up to $550.03 followed by an online buy from a brand-new device profile in a billing region the card had never used — while the decisive legitimacy evidence (memory family) is a near-zero case-memory score (cms_p 0.0054 versus the raw risk_score of 0.77) and a prior cleared risk alert on this same card, CC-1313, resolved as confirmed travel; two other prior closed cases on the card, CC-3886 and CC-0615, were confirmed card_not_present_new_device fraud, so the alternative reading — that this is simply a repeat of that confirmed pattern rather than a false alarm — remains live. We requested step-up authentication on the online purchase; the reply is assumed inconclusive/no response within the window, so per R4 the recommendation is CREATE_CASE, MONITOR_CARD, DECLINE_TRANSACTION on the pending $599.94 authorization (L1 route, exposure $2,140.94 ≤ $2,500), and ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST for a human to resolve the conflict; no SAR is filed at this stage. If a step-up reply arrives, a pass closes the case per R3 and a fail triggers BLOCK_CARD per R2.
